Replay

Slopball3D Parties and browser play

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Profiles, authority and savesVerificationReopening a saved party

Configure a Replay Room service to expose Create party, Join party, Watch only, Copy invite and Rejoin recent in the 3D game. Native and browser builds use the same Party/Room adapters. Without a service, native direct Host/Join/Watch remain available; Solo uses a local session.

Use separate terminals for the local service and game:

Shell
mkdir -m 700 -p .replay-slopball3d-data
REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT=0x52534c4f50334434 REPLAY_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MODEL=slopball3d \
REPLAY_ROOM_DB="$PWD/.replay-slopball3d-data/rooms.sqlite3" \
REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1 REPLAY_ROOM_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_room_service/run.sh
Shell
RS3_ROOM_SERVICE=ws://127.0.0.1:49740 RS3_ROOM_LOCAL=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_slopball3d/play.sh

Omit database creation when reopening an existing service. A service selects one content ID; use separate service ports/databases for different games.

Create a party and share its invite. Other players paste it and Join, selecting Watch only for an observer. The first connected player starts the match. WASD moves on XZ, Space kicks with loft, Enter opens chat and Tab shows the scoreboard.

Native launch options use RS3_*. Browser URL parameters use the lowercase suffix, including room_service, room_local, name, port and latency. Browser multiplayer uses RTC and a configured Party service. The profile loads before connection controls become available.

Profiles, authority and saves#

Personal identity/name preferences use replay-slopball3d; Party credentials use replay-slopball3d-rooms. Native Party data defaults to user://slopball3d_rooms.sqlite3, overridden by RS3_ROOMS_DB. Browser identity/name/credentials use the shared IndexedDB adapters. Rejoin uses the stored Party credential and a new process incarnation, preserving the member independently of personal preferences.

Invites admit up to three trusted peers who may host. Watch only selects seat zero, disables succession-checkpoint acceptance, and keeps the observer's ball solver frozen. Handoff is available when the authority has an eligible successor.

Migration restores the approved complete checkpoint under a newer epoch. Body3 seeds the owner solver from saved position, quaternion orientation and linear/angular velocity. Fresh observations use the new ownership scope. An abrupt host loss may roll back to the approved backup. Godot contact caches and joints are not serialized.

Save/F5 in a Party publishes through the service and reports a committed receipt. RS3_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MS optionally requests automatic publication. A later save replaces the room's published progress. This is separate from native direct file Save/Resume and does not create browser-local game-save slots. Browser-local Solo saves are described in the session guide.

RS3_ROOM_ADDRESS/RS3_PORT describe native gameplay reachability (default 49580). RS3_ROOM_CA supplies a native trusted certificate; RS3_ICE_JSON and RS3_ROOM_RELAY configure the existing RTC/relay adapters. The explicit RS3_ROOM_LOCAL=1 exception permits WS only on literal loopback addresses. Public browser deployment requires the normal secure service/origin and reachable ICE setup.

The operator-selected slopball3d backend validates D4 (0x52534c4f50334434) checkpoints. Client requests cannot choose validation code. The integration changes no game model, schema, physics material, collision shape, camera or mesh geometry.

Verification#

Shell
REPLAY_SLOPBALL3D_ONLINE_OUT=/absolute/fresh/output \
  nix develop --command bash tests/replay_slopball3d_online/run.sh

The fixture exercises native Party UI and four-browser planned/crash migration, checking complete spinning backups, solver pose/momentum, new kicks/goals, observer rejoin, fresh old-host return, retained/new named chat, common world digests, service publication, RTC traffic, graphics errors and control layout. RS3_PROBE=1 enables the checkpoint diagnostics used by the fixture. Public/Steam deployment, broader hardware/failure sequences and human gameplay comparison remain roadmap work.

See recorded results and limitations.

Reopening a saved party#

Rejoin recent can restore the service's published progress after every game process and the service stop. Keep the service database and returning members' credentials; restart the service with database creation disabled. Either the original creator or another trusted saved player can restore. In Watch mode, an observer may register first but does not start an authority runtime. Other players return to their saved seats, and the original creator can rejoin after a different member has restored the party.

The new authority installs the exact published world under a newer epoch. Body3 seeds from the saved position, quaternion, linear velocity and angular velocity before new scoped observations commit. The UI reports restored progress and known rolled-back ticks. Continuing play can publish a replacement checkpoint. Progress after publication and cosmetic chat history can be lost after total process loss; solver contact caches and joints are not serialized.

The native WSS test and browser RTC test test both returning-host choices, independently decode source and replacement publications, and compare the actual first solver seed before requiring another kick and goal.

See the expanded recovery matrix and its limits.

The recovery notice uses the shared backup-status observation. It distinguishes an approved backup from preparation, stale progress or uncertain control; a prior host change does not imply the next backup is ready.
